title: Grain Desk Standing Rule: The Forward Reserve Held Back Before Delivery Begins
content:
The forward reserve is bushels of headroom the desk holds back on a contract under Grain Marketing Contracts whose delivery has not begun, and it is taken off the marketing ceiling.

**1.** Where the contract's delivery window has opened and at least one load stands against it, no forward reserve is held back.

**2.** Where the delivery window has not opened but opens inside the near window of 90 calendar days, the reserve is 1500 bushels.

**3.** Where neither of those holds, the reserve is 3000 bushels.

## The three cases side by side

| The contract's delivery window | Loads standing against the contract | Reserve held back |
|---|---|---|
| Has opened | at least one | none |
| Has opened | none | 3000 bushels |
| Has not opened, and opens within 90 calendar days | either way | 1500 bushels |
| Has not opened, and opens more than 90 calendar days out | either way | 3000 bushels |

A window that opens today counts as opened. A window opening on the ninetieth day from today is inside the near window, that figure itself qualifying; one opening on the ninety-first day is outside it and the reserve is 3000 bushels.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A ceiling struck at 42,000 bushels on a contract whose window opened last week and against which two loads stand loses nothing to the reserve. The same ceiling on a contract whose window opens in six weeks becomes 40,500 bushels. On a contract whose window opens in five months it becomes 39,000 bushels.
